# Requirements Quality Checklist: End-to-end minimum viable product

**Purpose**: Reviewer check of the whole specification, including the clarifications, before the specification gate. Focus areas: stage gates and evidence, untrusted input and authorization, and human-readable output. Depth: standard.
**Created**: 2026-10-27
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Reviewer notes**: The notes below were added by hand by the Product Owner agent after the first review pass. They are not an independent review and no item is checked. "Addressed by hand edit" means the specification was changed to answer the question; "Open" means the question is deferred to the stage named in the note. Only an independent reviewer may check an item.

## Stage gates and evidence: completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Does every stage in the eleven-stage list have a named gate, or is it stated which stages are gated only by FR-036's generic wording? [Completeness, Spec §User Story 1, FR-036]
  - Reviewer note: Open: each stage's gate is named in its stage contract at architecture time (FR-036 requires one); an independent reviewer should confirm that is enough.
- [ ] CHK002 Is the pass criterion defined for the plan gate, the specification gate and the readability gate, beyond the checks they must perform? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012, FR-015, FR-034]
  - Reviewer note: Open: pass criteria for the specification, plan and readability gates belong to the gate definitions written at architecture time.
- [ ] CHK003 Is the "evidence hash" defined well enough to say what is hashed and when it is computed? [Clarity, Spec §FR-019, Key Entities]
  - Reviewer note: Open: what is hashed and when is a design decision for the evidence manifest.
- [ ] CHK004 Are requirements for rework defined for the documentation stage, as FR-039 does for the technical review? [Gap, Spec §FR-039, FR-026]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-039 now gives documentation the same two-round limit.
- [ ] CHK005 Is the order of the documentation review and the documentation quality gate stated, including what happens when code changes during rework after docs were written? [Gap, Spec §User Story 8, FR-039]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-026 sets the order and FR-039 requires a documentation re-check after code changes.
- [ ] CHK006 Are the stage budgets and timeouts quantified, or is it clear that the stage contract will supply them? [Clarity, Spec §FR-036, Assumptions]
  - Reviewer note: Open: budgets and timeouts come from each stage contract; a human should confirm that is acceptable for Slice 1.
- [ ] CHK007 Is the meaning of "checklist state" in the specification gate defined, including which checklist files count and what state blocks the gate? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-012]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-012 now defines checklist state.
- [ ] CHK008 Are the four check statuses (passed, failed, blocked, not applicable) defined once and used consistently across checks, gates and documentation results? [Consistency, Spec §FR-020, FR-026, Key Entities]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-020 now defines the four result states once.
- [ ] CHK009 Is it stated how a gate decision is recorded, and what it must contain, so that a reviewer can tell evidence from assertion? [Gap, Spec §FR-012, FR-032]
  - Reviewer note: Open: the record format of a gate decision is a contract design; FR-012 already requires evidence.

## Stage gates and evidence: consistency and measurability

- [ ] CHK010 Is "a verified gate decision" in FR-032 consistent with the stages that have no deterministic gate, such as intake classification and the independent review? [Consistency, Spec §FR-032, FR-005, FR-023]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-032 now requires a gate to validate agent output.
- [ ] CHK011 Do the "blocked" outcomes in FR-020, FR-036 and FR-038 describe one state, or three different ones? [Consistency, Spec §FR-020, FR-036, FR-038]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-020 now defines blocked as one state.
- [ ] CHK012 Can "natural English" and "claims match the implemented behaviour" be objectively measured as written? [Measurability, Spec §FR-026, SC-009]
  - Reviewer note: Open: thresholds for natural English and claim matching belong to the documentation gate definition.
- [ ] CHK013 Is each success criterion that depends on a "seeded" defect or input tied to a defined set of seeded cases, so the percentages are checkable? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003, SC-006, SC-009]
  - Reviewer note: Open: the seeded cases must be listed as evaluation fixtures during planning.
- [ ] CHK014 Is SC-001's "single unattended run" consistent with the one-question intake path and the two rework rounds? [Conflict, Spec §SC-001, FR-006, FR-039]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: SC-001 now excludes the question and escalation paths.
- [ ] CHK015 Are the requirement numbers and their order consistent, given that FR-038 and FR-039 appear out of sequence? [Consistency, Spec §FR-024, FR-037, FR-038, FR-039]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-037 to FR-040 are now in numeric order.

## Untrusted input and authorization

- [ ] CHK016 Does the rule that instructions are treated as data cover every untrusted source named in the constitution (dependency contents, documentation, web pages, tool output and model output), or only issue text and repository files? [Gap, Spec §FR-004]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-004 now lists every untrusted source.
- [ ] CHK017 Is it defined who the "authorized human" is in FR-007, and whether this is the same allowlist as in FR-001? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007, FR-001]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-001 and FR-007 tie overrides to operators on the same allowlist.
- [ ] CHK018 Is the operator's authority to approve, reject, pause, request rework or cancel tied to an authorization rule, as the requester's is? [Gap, Spec §FR-029]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-029 requires an operator designation check on each action.
- [ ] CHK019 Are the requirements clear on when authorization is checked, given the edge case about a person losing authorization after filing? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, Edge Cases]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-001 checks authorization at acceptance and before the draft pull request.
- [ ] CHK020 Is the content of a rejection message limited so that it does not reveal the allowlist or other internal detail to an unauthorized person? [Gap, Spec §FR-002]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-002 forbids revealing the allowlist or internal detail.
- [ ] CHK021 Is the audit record's content and protection defined (what is recorded, who can read it, and that it cannot be changed)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, Key Entities]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-002 defines audit record content and append-only protection.
- [ ] CHK022 Is "separately from the normalized request" specific enough to test, for example by stating that no later stage reads the original text as instructions? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-003 says later stages receive the original text only as quoted data.
- [ ] CHK023 Are requirements defined for an issue that is edited after acceptance, beyond the edge-case statement? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, FR-003, FR-013]
  - Reviewer note: Open: an edited issue is covered by an edge case and FR-013; an independent reviewer should decide whether it needs its own numbered requirement.
- [ ] CHK024 Does a functional requirement exist for the edge case of duplicate delivery of the same issue event? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-040 covers duplicate delivery.
- [ ] CHK025 Are the secret-handling edge case and FR-035 backed by an acceptance scenario that a tester could run? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, FR-035]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: Story 6 scenario 6 covers secret scanning.
- [ ] CHK026 Is the boundary of "protected" paths and configuration defined, including who sets them and where the list is recorded? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-009, FR-018, FR-021]
  - Reviewer note: Open: who sets the protected paths and where they are recorded is policy design (FR-009, FR-018, FR-021).

## Human-readable output

- [ ] CHK027 Is the readability gate's scope listed, covering which artifacts it reads (issue comments, specification, plan, pull request, documentation) and which findings are warnings versus blocks? [Completeness, Spec §FR-034]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-034 lists the artifacts in scope and says only clear violations block.
- [ ] CHK028 Is there an acceptance scenario for FR-034's readability gate, as there are for the other gates? [Gap, Spec §FR-034, User Stories]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: Story 5 scenario 4 covers the readability gate.
- [ ] CHK029 Are the title rules in FR-016 extended to the pull request title, the issue comments and the documentation headings, or only to task titles? [Coverage, Spec §FR-016, FR-008, FR-034]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-034 now covers comments, titles, pull request text and documentation headings.
- [ ] CHK030 Is "short" quantified for titles, or is a deliberate absence of a length limit stated? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016]
  - Reviewer note: Open: a title length limit is a readability gate setting.
- [ ] CHK031 Are the plain-English requirements for failure comments specific about content (stage, reason, next step) and tone? [Clarity, Spec §FR-038]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-038 now requires stage, reason and next step.
- [ ] CHK032 Is the rule that quoted text and domain terms stay untranslated consistent with the rule that all human-facing text is English? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, FR-034]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-034 now marks quoted text and domain terms as quotations.
- [ ] CHK033 Can "preserving the technical intent" for Portuguese requests be objectively checked, and is the "independent reader" in SC-010 defined? [Measurability, Spec §FR-008, SC-010]
  - Reviewer note: Open: the intent-preservation check and the independent reader are defined with the Portuguese fixture.

## Scope, assumptions and dependencies

- [ ] CHK034 Are the out-of-scope items listed only in Edge Cases consistent with the requirement that the factory decline or block requests needing them? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases, FR-037]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-037 requires declining or blocking out-of-scope requests; the list stays in Edge Cases to keep the canonical sections.
- [ ] CHK035 Is the assumption that a command-line or pull-request-comment interface exists for the operator reflected in a requirement, or only in Assumptions? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, FR-029]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: FR-029 now names the command line and pull request comments.
- [ ] CHK036 Are the dependencies on the installed Spec Kit, the sandbox and GitHub credentials stated with the required behaviour when each is unavailable? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions, Edge Cases, FR-010]
  - Reviewer note: Addressed by hand edit: the Assumptions now state what happens when the sandbox or credentials are unavailable.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
